title: Equal Material Huh?
summary: Use a bishop interposition to lure the defender into blocking its own queen, then threaten mate from two directions.

nodes.question: What matters more than the equal queen-and-bishop material?
nodes.explanation: White’s king restricts Kh8, but immediate queen checks let Black coordinate its defenders. Bd3 prepares the bishop’s blocking role.

nodes.question: Why is the black bishop useful to White on f6?
nodes.explanation: It blocks the queen’s route along the f-file to Kf7. White can now threaten Qh5 and Qe8 without allowing the source’s perpetual-check defense.

branches.title: Lure the bishop and switch the queen’s attack
commentary: Begin from the complete six-piece source board. The main line follows the illustrated queen check and bishop interference.
Bd3 offers the bishop and prepares to answer ...Qh5+ with Bg6, keeping the white king in its restricting position.
Qh5+ uses Black’s available queen check to try to force that king away.
Bg6 interposes while attacking the checking queen on h5.
Qh4 retreats along the h-file and keeps the queen available for defense.
Qb2+ checks on the long diagonal and deliberately invites the bishop to block.
Bf6 blocks that diagonal, but also obstructs Black’s own queen’s access to the f-file.
Qb5 switches threats toward Qh5 and Qe8. The bishop on f6 prevents the queen from checking Kf7 along that file.
Qe1 is the illustrated queen defense against the eighth-rank attack, leaving h5 available.
Qh5# is actual mate. Bg6 supports h5 and covers h7, while Kf7 restricts g7 and g8.
branches.explanation: Qh5# is actual mate. Bg6 supports h5 and covers h7, while Kf7 restricts g7 and g8.

branches.title: Move the blocking bishop
commentary: Compare the source’s bishop move from the final attacking setup.
Bd8 abandons the f6 interference square but cannot cover the queen’s entry on e8.
Qe8# is actual mate along the eighth rank. Kf7 covers g8 and Bg6 covers h7; Black cannot interpose its queen from h4.
branches.explanation: Qe8# is actual mate along the eighth rank. Kf7 covers g8 and Bg6 covers h7; Black cannot interpose its queen from h4.

branches.title: Capture the offered bishop
commentary: Compare the source’s direct acceptance of the first bishop offer.
Bd3 offers a bishop to divert the queen from its initial defensive arrangement.
Qxd3 collects that bishop but leaves White a decisive queen check.
Qb2+ attacks the king along the long diagonal.
Kh7 is the sole legal reply in this exact position.
Qg7# is actual mate. Kf7 protects g7 and denies the adjacent escape squares, while the queen covers the h-file flights.
branches.explanation: Qg7# is actual mate. Kf7 protects g7 and denies the adjacent escape squares, while the queen covers the h-file flights.

branches.title: Start checking before organizing the bishop
commentary: Compare the source’s first tempting queen check.
Qb8+ gives up the forced win. White has not arranged the bishop interference.
Qd8 blocks the check and holds the exact position drawn with best play. The lesson stops before inventing a further forcing sequence.
branches.explanation: Qd8 blocks the check and holds the exact position drawn with best play. The lesson stops before inventing a further forcing sequence.

exercises.prompt: Why lure the bishop onto f6 instead of taking it?
exercises.answer: On f6 it obstructs Black’s queen. White can switch between two mating routes without allowing the f-file checking resource.
It blocks the check and attacks the queen while keeping Kf7 close enough to restrict the black king.

startContext: The complete six-piece source board is visually reconstructed. The bishop offer, ...Qh5+ interposition, ...Bf6 lure and two final mating defenses are checked move by move. Immediate Qb8+ is checked as drawing. The selected branches do not enumerate every legal queen defense.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
